objective: Over abstract names, to be proved: (L1) in a world whose components are finite, a finite change is a renaming exactly when it keeps the multiset of isomorphism types of the components it touches, so a change of values on one copy of (B, c) is a renaming exactly when the new colouring is an automorphic image of c; (L2) in a world of infinite trees no change of values alone is a renaming; (L3) the switch flips a neighbour distinction by a minimal change of neighbour distinctions alone that is not a renaming, when the edge lies on a cycle of a finite component or in a tree world; (L4) when values and neighbour distinctions change together, a place can be transplanted by a finite rewiring that is not a renaming, so a count that excludes only renamings still excludes little, and the operative count holds the board fixed for values; (L5) in the laws that never put a 0 beside a 1, and in law 48, no finite change of values alone flips a value in a tree world.
status: Proved 2026-11-10 (read before publication by an independent referee; fixes made): renamings in worlds of finite components are the changes that keep component types; on four-regular trees no change of values alone is a renaming; the switch flips neighbour distinctions in place; transplants make excluding renamings alone insufficient, so flips are counted in place (A60); where no allowed state has a mixed edge, and in law 48, values cannot flip by finite changes on infinite components; least fixed points (after the census) decide value flips on trees. Checks passed: all 90 board-value knots native in place in some world of finite pieces; on trees 26 native in place, 64 not.
title: Renamings, transplants and flips in place
